issues.description: The 15 supplied R programs expose named PostgreSQL relations, many consumed fields and join keys, sample filters, and authored transformations. This package does not provide the PostgreSQL connection/database settings or loading handoffs for those external relations, and the compatible table contents, field types/units, and required history are not verified. The README explicitly places StreetEvents transcript parsing and non-answer, linguistic-feature, and NER feature creation outside this shared code note, leaving those required upstream producers and their compatible inputs unresolved.

Both create_crsp_calls.R and create_sp1500.R consume the project relation hpr_link, but none of the supplied programs creates it. Its exact schema, construction recipe, and compatible local route remain unresolved.

The complete main-results analysis is embedded as R snippets in a PDF note rather than a standalone driver. Extract and reflow the snippets in order in a working copy, preserving the authored helper functions, model definitions, and handoffs before attempting execution.

The two packaged .RData files are identified by the author as prepared call-level and question-answer-level estimation inputs and are loaded by the embedded analysis, but their object names, columns, identifiers, period, and compatibility could not be established through safe bounded non-evaluating metadata. Do not deserialize them for this static assessment; retain the analysis-input contract as unresolved.

evidence.quote:
This note describes the code shared in glz_share/glz_create_data that creates the
final estimation data from raw data. All code is written in R.

evidence.description: The README lists upstream transcript parsing and feature-generation code as outside the shared note.

The code beyond the scope of this note:
   • StreetEvents conference calls data parsing code https://github.com/iangow/se_core
   • Non-answer creation code https://github.com/iangow/ling_features/blob/master/
     non_answer/non_answers.py
   • In- and out-of-sample performance of non-answer code https://github.com/iangow/

evidence.description: The README describes the linked-data step, independent Step 1 producers, merged data, and final estimation tables.
evidence.quote:
Given the raw data from various sources described in the paper, the shared code should
be executed in the following sequence:

evidence.description: The README identifies HPR calls as a proprietary input used by CRSP-call and S&P 1500 construction; the native programs consume hpr_link.
evidence.quote:
• create_crsp_calls.R creates stock market variables and Black-Scholes param-
    eters as of call date. Uses CRSP data and link to HPR calls. The HPR calls data is
    proprietary provided by the authors of Hollander et al. (2010).
  • create_crsp_fye.R creates stock market variables and Black-Scholes parameters
    as of fiscal year end date. Uses Equilar and CRSP data.
  • create_ciq_offerings.R creates debt/equity issuance based on Capital IQ key
    developments. Uses Capital IQ data.
  • create_rscript.R pulls together spontaneity measure from Lee (2016). Uses
    StreetEvents and linguistic features data extracted from StreetEvents. Script measure
    is computed following description in Lee (2016).
  • create_sp1500.R creates SP1500 membership data (including HPR calls in
    hpr_link). Uses Compustat data.

evidence.description: The analysis note says its R snippets reproduce main results without Equilar controls and with anonymized identifiers/dates.
evidence.quote:
This note replicates main results in the paper “Non-answers during Conference Calls” by Gow, Larcker, and Zakolyukina without
control variables for data shared in glz_share/glz_knit_tables. All code snippets are written in R.
To protect proprietary data, we have done the following:
   • Omitted control variables, which contain data from Equilar
   • Replaced firm identifiers with cik, which is a Central Index Key (CIK) used on the SEC’s computer systems to identify
     corporations
   • Replaced StreetEvents transcript identifiers with random file_name_alt and omitted dates of conference calls

actions.description: Before the full raw-data branch can be attempted, configure the PostgreSQL connection and compatible source-table loading handoffs, resolve the outside-scope feature producers and missing hpr_link handoff, and confirm only unresolved data contracts without changing the authored transformations.
steps: Configure the PostgreSQL connection, project role/schema access, and nonans_product search_path. For every source relation in probes/workflow_trace.json, use the fields, join keys, filters, and transformations exposed by the supplied SQL/R code as the starting contract; confirm only remaining physical types, units, compatible feature vintage, population, and date/history coverage.

Consider the cataloged local SAS raw-product candidates for source preparation: COMP.FUNDA, COMP.FUNDQ, COMP.CO_HGIC, COMP.SEC_HISTORY, CRSP.DSF, COMP.IDXCST_HIS, CIQ.WRDS_KEYDEV, IBES.ACTU_EPSUS, and IBES.DETU_EPSUS. The exact mapped Compustat, CRSP.DSF, and CIQ fields plus cataloged SAS type/length/format metadata are recorded in the linked lookup; establish a deliberate PostgreSQL field/type/label conversion and vintage/history crosswalk before using any candidate. These are inventory candidates only, with no live file read, DB load, period proof, access check, or license-denial finding.

Keep specific unmatched contracts open: the lookup did not identify an exact CRSP.MSE, IBES.ID, COMP.IDX_INDEX, or Fama-French industry_49 table; COMP.IDXCST_HIS lacks the source-required fromdt name; IBES actuals/detail files are raw candidates whose variable/format mapping to the author's prepared relations remains unknown. FF.FACTORS_DAILY and FF.FACTORS_MONTHLY are factor files, not the required 49-industry SIC bounds. Execucomp aggregate tables are cataloged but are not established substitutes for the Equilar company_fyear, executives, and equity_calc inputs. No matching Comtrade, HPR, StreetEvents, non-answer, or language/NER feature product was identified in this bounded catalog search.

Identify author-compatible producers and inputs for the outside-scope StreetEvents parsing, non-answer, linguistic-feature, and Stanford NER tables. Resolve the separate hpr_link handoff: confirm its required fields, join coverage, provenance, and compatible mapping for create_crsp_calls.R and create_sp1500.R without assigning it an unsupported producer.

Follow the supplied stage order in probes/workflow_trace.json: create_se_link produces se_link; create_nonans_rate, create_nonans_ner, and create_comp_rate consume se_link and produce their feature relations; create_fundann, create_fundqtr, create_ibes_mb, create_crsp_calls, create_crsp_fye, create_ciq_offerings, create_rscript, and create_sp1500 produce the named intermediate relations; create_calls_merged consumes those outputs plus the named external relations and produces calls_merged; create_calls_set produces calls_set; create_ner_set consumes se_link, nonans_ner, and calls_set and produces ner_set. Retain create_crsp_fye as a supplied output-producing stage even though no supplied source reads its result.
Preserve all authored PostgreSQL transformations, fiscal/date filters, sample definitions, winsorization, fixed effects, and model handoffs after the remaining input contracts are resolved.
validation: For each selected cataloged SAS candidate, verify a field-by-field name/type/format/label conversion into the expected PostgreSQL source relation and check compatible population, source vintage, and required date history before using it.
Statically reconcile every relation read and written by all 15 programs against the ordered producer-consumer map before any later authorized run.
For the hhi/fluid joined input, verify which source or compatible mapping supplies post-join tnic3tsimm before treating the required field contract as resolved.

review_notes: Static review covers all 15 supplied PostgreSQL-backed R programs, the complete embedded analysis note, the author data-sheet, and workflow documentation. The full pipeline retains every supplied stage, including create_crsp_fye, and remains unresolved for compatible upstream relation contents, outside-scope transcript/non-answer/feature producers, hpr_link, PostgreSQL setup, and the post-join tnic3tsimm source mapping.

The separate prepared-data analysis route is supported by the author's calls_set_glz.RData and ner_set_glz.RData candidates and embedded analysis code. It reproduces the documented modified main-results branch without Equilar controls, using CIK and randomized file_name_alt identifiers while omitting call dates; it is not full-original equivalence. Both RData schemas and compatibility remain unknown because no deserialization was performed.

The bounded frozen catalog lookup identifies candidate local SAS source tables for Compustat annual/quarterly data, GICS/security history, CRSP daily stock data, CIQ key-development events, IBES raw actuals/detail files, and index constituent history. It records metadata-backed field/format matches where available; it does not establish data readability, product entitlement, PostgreSQL conversion, actual time coverage, or compatible author-specific prepared-feature contracts. Cataloged Fama-French factor files are not a substitute for the required industry_49 classification, and the source-required fromdt field was not identified in the cataloged COMP.IDXCST_HIS candidate.

Only runtime/package metadata and the frozen workspace catalog were inspected. No author program was sourced, loaded, compiled, or run; no database query, package installation, dataset read/download/construction, RData deserialization, regression, or model was performed. R 4.5.0 is available, while ten exact R packages were absent from the selected runtime's default library paths.
